summary: Tou-hui Fok was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at New Asia College (~1960–1966), New Asia Institute (~1964–1966), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1966–1969), and Otani University (1969). He taught at CUHK (~1972–1982).
Tracy Franz is an educator in Buddhist studies and other fields. In 2018, she held teaching posts at Dalhousie University and Shokei University.

Indology and religious studies scholar Travis L. Smith studied at UC Berkeley under Vasudha Dalmia, Robert P. Goldman, and Sally J. Sutherland Goldman, and earned a PhD from Columbia (2007) under John Stratton Hawley. He held posts at Barnard and Florida.
Trent Walker is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Alexander von Rospatt.
Trevor Leggett worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied law at King's College London (~1931–1934) and served as Head of the Japanese Service at the BBC (~1946–1970).

Trijang Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He taught at Ganden Shartse Monastery and instructed the 14th Dalai Lama, Zong Rinpoche, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Troy Organ was a philosophy and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Iowa (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Parsons College (~1944–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), Ohio University (1954), and Chatham University.
Trung Huynh is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at University of the West under the supervision of Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1997–2004), studying under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Thomas Burke.

Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Oxford under Richard Gombrich (-2004). He conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow (1987). He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and was appointed Instructor in Tibetan at the University of Oxford in 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya is a historian and Tibetologist who studied at SOAS University of London (~1978–2004). He held posts at SOAS (~1990–2007) and the University of British Columbia (~2007), where he became a professor.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Adeu Rinpoche (~1990–2007). He taught Adam Pearcey.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi studied at Kyoto, Penn, and Indiana (PhD 1994) under Nishida, Sato, Kajiyama, Nagao, Kelsang, Hoffmann, Beckwith, Norbu, and Sperling. A linguist and Tibetologist, he was Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University (~1999–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo studied at the University of Tokyo (~1959–1967). He lectured at Rissho University (~1970–1975, ~1980–1985) and served as President of Reiyūkai (~1977–1993, ~1996–2013) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1977–2019).
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung earned a PhD in Buddhist studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He attended Toyama Chubu High School (~1968–1971) and held academic posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1980–1998) and the University of Tokyo (~1998–2018).

Tsultrim Allione studied at Antioch University (MA ~1980–1982) and under Abo Rinpoche, Chögyam Trungpa, and Namkhai Norbu. A Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner who taught Ryan Matthew Jacobson, she founded Tara Mandala.

Tsultrim Gyatso was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).
